# TravelPal.now weekly newsletter

Send Saturday at 09:00 America/Los_Angeles, first regular issue October 10, 2026. The user authorized the October 3 test to both existing subscribed addresses (both belong to the user), then regular weekly delivery to newsletter subscribers.

The existing website publish workflow compiles and uploads a seven-day draft artifact; no new GitHub workflow or paid discovery requests. Run `python3 scripts/weekly_digest.py` for HTML and provenance JSON. Latest finalized revisions win; inactive stories and repeated story IDs are excluded. Do not pad quiet weeks with old articles or call an empty edition a full week of news. Links retain original sources and the published brief. Only use already published briefs and their verified facts.

The existing GitHub workflow also runs Saturday at 09:00 America/Los_Angeles, independent of a local computer. GitHub schedules are best effort and may be delayed. **This compiles a draft; it does not send email yet.** The former local Codex/browser sender is paused at the user's request and must not be reactivated as a substitute for cloud delivery.

EmailOctopus's current v2 API cannot create campaigns, but supports queueing contacts into a dashboard-created API-started automation with repeat entry enabled. That is the supported cloud delivery path under evaluation. Starter allows seven additional custom fields, each text value limited to 600 characters, so the full HTML digest cannot be transported this way. The proposed alternative is four topic highlights in the email linking to the full weekly digest on TravelPal.now. Await the user's format selection before changing the newsletter. Do not truncate the current digest silently or use undocumented campaign endpoints.

Before enabling cloud delivery: configure and test the native repeating automation; secure its API credential in GitHub Actions secrets; verify rendering with the user's test contacts; and implement durable issue/recipient deduplication and quota checks. Credentials and subscriber addresses must not appear in public artifacts, logs or history. References: [v2 API](https://emailoctopus.com/api-documentation/v2), [field limits](https://help.emailoctopus.com/article/37-adding-new-fields), [repeating automations](https://help.emailoctopus.com/article/379-repeating-an-automation).

Daily publication is a separate unfinished prerequisite. Verified October 3: the website's TRAVEL_BRIEFS_ENABLED variable is false; the CardPecker Azure app's SHARED_TRAVEL_POLICY_ENABLED and TRAVEL_BRIEFS_ENABLED settings are false. Its collection schedule does not establish automatic blog publication. The approved October 3 edition is published, but new automatic editions require source coverage repair and live quality validation before activation. See the server's docs/source-and-quality-review.md. Do not promise seven fresh editions before this path is operational.

Free Starter only: no paid plans, trials, add-ons, extra users or removal of provider branding. Before sending verify current subscribed contacts <= 2500 and monthly sends + this issue <= 10000. Capacity must be available, not assumed. Stop and notify if a send would exceed either limit. At 2500 contacts, five weekly sends exceed the monthly allowance; skip rather than upgrade. Retain unsubscribe and sender address merge fields plus provider branding.

Use a unique issue key TravelPal.now Weekly YYYY-MM-DD. Cloud delivery needs durable storage for per-issue and per-recipient enqueue outcomes before activation; the earlier local test ledger is not a cloud deduplication solution. Never duplicate a sent or scheduled issue, including after timeouts. Retain period, story IDs, content digest and provider-confirmed status. Follow any new user corrections before the next edition. No newsletter sends on other days without authorization.
